props.title: The Dragon Lives Again

sections.content: **The Dragon Lives Again (1977)** (1977) stands as one of the most bizarrely fascinating "Bruceploitation" films made after Bruce Lee's death. This surreal Hong Kong action comedy features "Bruce Lee" (played by Bruce Leung) arriving in the underworld where he teams up with Popeye and Kwai Chang Caine to battle Dracula, James Bond, the Godfather, and other pop culture icons. It perfectly captures the wild exploitation era of 1970s Hong Kong cinema, when filmmakers rushed to cash in on Lee's legacy with lookalike actors and increasingly outlandish plots. Like Game of Death (1978) and **Tower of Death** (1981), it represents the fascinating phenomenon of posthumous Bruce Lee films.

sections.content: The "Bruceploitation" wave produced over 200 films between 1973-1981, featuring actors like Bruce Li, Bruce Le, and Dragon Lee. While most attempted serious martial arts action like **Fist of Fury 2** (1977) and **Exit the Dragon, Enter the Tiger** (1976), **The Dragon Lives Again** took the surreal comedy route. It's part of a subset of wilder Bruceploitation films including **The Clones of Bruce Lee** (1977), where Bruce Lee clones fight a mad scientist, and **Bruce Lee Fights Back from the Grave** (1976), featuring a zombie Bruce Lee.

Beyond its exploitation roots, the film reflects Hong Kong cinema's creative approach to copyright and pop culture mashups. Similar to how **Mad Mad Kung Fu** (1976) and **Stranger from Shaolin** (1977) freely mixed genres and borrowed characters, **The Dragon Lives Again** throws together a stew of unlicensed Western and Eastern characters with gleeful disregard for intellectual property. This mashup mentality would later influence films like Kung Fu Hustle (2004) and **Shaolin Soccer** (2001). SUBHEAD: Impact on Modern Cinema

sections.content: The irreverent spirit of films like **The Dragon Lives Again** lives on in modern martial arts comedies and pop culture mashups. **Kung Pow: Enter the Fist** (2002) directly parodies both Bruce Lee films and Bruceploitation tropes. Meanwhile, **Black Dynamite** (2009) lovingly spoofs both kung fu and blaxploitation films of the 1970s, showing how this era's wild creativity continues to inspire filmmakers.
